proved.name: proved
proved.says: A law in the Lean model holds it, pinned by test vectors. The listed laws hold under their premises; that is not a proof of every product surface.

designed.name: designed
designed.says: Decided in the design, and not built yet. It is not a ruling.

open.name: open
open.says: Waiting on a ruling. See Decisions.

groups.name: The ground
groups.gist: What was said, and by whom.

groups.name: Holding
groups.gist: Where records are kept, and what one reader has.

groups.name: Asking
groups.gist: A standing question, and the answer worked out from records.

groups.name: A moment
groups.gist: An answer fixed so others can cite it.

groups.name: Text
groups.gist: The answer as something people read and edit.

nouns.purpose: One thing an observer saw, written so anyone can check it and nobody can change it.
nouns.principle: Its id is a hash of what it says, written one canonical way. Spell a set in another order and the id stays. Erase the payload and the id, the signature and every record that cites it still hold.
nouns.eg: Every card in the walk is a record.
nouns.state: An envelope, a payload and a signature. A fold reads the top-level fields of a payload it holds: a list reads as a set, no field name is special, and nothing reads inside a nested object. The id is a hash of the envelope and of a commitment to the payload.

nouns.principle: Nothing a record says is true. It is said, by its observer. Two observers who disagree leave two records, and both are kept.
nouns.eg: Rosa, Ben and Kim in the walk.
nouns.state: A typed reference on every record. Today it is the signing key, k:….
nouns.note: Lineages (sl:…), key bindings and standing come in step 3. What an observer names is open: IS10 and IS11.

nouns.purpose: Gives each subject its own state, within the records a reader has admitted.
nouns.principle: Inside a thing, a record that nothing replaces is a head. Two records that replace the same one make a fork. A record that names both heads merges them.
nouns.state: A typed name, prefix:value, in a record's of: a natural key or a record id. Every record is of exactly one thing. A record with no of and no prev is a root and starts a thing named by its own id. about only mentions other things.

nouns.purpose: Holds records, and nothing else. It owns no meaning.
nouns.principle: A store is a set. Where the copies of a record agree, read its places in any order and you keep the same records, once per id.
nouns.state: A set of records kept in places, each record one canonical line.

nouns.purpose: Lets readers who hold different payloads still agree on what is current.
nouns.principle: A reader who keeps every envelope keeps each thing's heads, whatever payloads are missing. A record that heads any thing stays among that reader's heads. Where a fold can't read a payload, it says how many it couldn't read.
nouns.eg: Kim's copy, which holds E without its payload.
nouns.state: What one reader holds: each record with its payload, withheld, or erased. Envelopes are always held.

nouns.purpose: A standing question, written as data anyone can check.
nouns.principle: An accepted spec parses back to itself. A refused one names the first rule it breaks, and where.
nouns.state: vertex names it, from lists its sources, fold lists its slots.

nouns.purpose: Chooses records by their envelopes alone.
nouns.principle: A source takes a record when its kind is listed, it mentions the thing in about, and it is of the thing in of, each only when given. A reader with fewer payloads takes exactly the same records.
nouns.state: A store, then optionally kinds, a thing it mentions (about) and the thing it is of.

nouns.principle: Hand each record over once, and the same records give every slot the same value, whatever order they came in. A slot over heads returns only records that are still heads, and a count, sum, min or max over heads folds every current record and nothing else. A slot with by splits what it selects into groups and accounts for every record it selected.
nouns.state: A name and one fold, optionally with where, follow, limit and by.

nouns.purpose: Turns a set of records into state.
nouns.principle: The read path hands each record over once. A fold whose steps can run in any order can take new records as they arrive and still reach the same state.
nouns.eg: latest-by picks the current recipe; count counts its versions.
nouns.state: One of six: count, sum, min, max, latest-by, collect. Following prev, a fold runs over each thing's heads. Following keys, it reads each thing by its live setters. Otherwise it runs over every selected record. The proofs over heads use cached latest-by state, not just a cached answer.

nouns.purpose: Asks a standing question over stores: select, fold, tick.
nouns.principle: Run it over the same set and it gives the same slots, each with a count of the records it couldn't read.
nouns.state: A spec, run over what a reader holds.
nouns.note: Designed and not built: naming a vertex by its spec's hash, and when it ticks.

nouns.purpose: Fixes a vertex's result at a moment, so others can cite it.
nouns.principle: Anyone who holds the covered records works out the same tick.
nouns.eg: Step 8 of the walk: one tick covering five records.
nouns.state: An ordinary record of kind tick: the vertex, the exact records it covers, and the result, with an id over all three. A tick folds a set named outright, a part closed downward over prev, or a slice of one.
nouns.note: Built in the model with its laws and vectors, in Rust, and in the CLI: loops tick writes one, and loops tick --check answers same, differs or cannot check. A tick made on one machine checks the same on another, and can cover a cut by time or by ids. Not built yet: boundaries, markers and the runner. The tick record note.

nouns.purpose: Turns state into text people edit, and edits back into records.
nouns.principle: With section ids that are nonempty and distinct, render, then parse, and you get the document back. Drop a section from the text and that section keeps its old body: leaving something out is never an edit.
nouns.eg: Step 9 of the walk, where Ben edits a section.
nouns.state: A render, a parse and a diff by ids, and the base the text came from.
nouns.note: The edit round trip also keeps exactly the base's ordered list of ids. Emitting accepted edits is planned.

nouns.purpose: Gives standing ahead of time, with a scope.
nouns.principle: A record without standing stays visible, and has no effect.
nouns.eg: Rosa's grant to Ben to write recipes in the family store.
nouns.state: A record. A record that acts on it names it in under.
nouns.note: What a grant holds, how it ends and who may give one wait on IS3, IS4, IS5 and IS7.

verbs.says: Check a record, sign it, and add it to a store. loops emit also fills in what a writer's tool may: the thing, the keys it sets, every live record of the thing, and the heads' about and occurred.
Fix a vertex's result at a boundary, as a value anyone can work out again.
Say no, with a code from a closed set and the path to what broke the rule. Never guess.
Where a record's forms agree, bring them together, one per id. Keep a payload any place holds, unless a held record erases it.
Refuse records that aren't entitled to their prev. Standing joins this check in step 3.
A source takes the records its store, kinds, mention and thing choose.
A where test answers yes, no, or unknown when the reader lacks the payload. present means the field was written. On a list, is asks whether a member equals the value, and no bound holds.
Walk prev inside a thing to its heads, the records nothing replaces. Following keys, read a thing by its live setters: for each key, the setters nothing above replaces.

Split what a slot selects by a key read from each record: its kind, its observer, what it mentions under a prefix, or a payload field. A payload list puts the record in one group per member. Always after settling, admission and the heads.
Turn what was taken into a slot's value.
Write state as keyed sections, each with a nonempty, distinct id. Views shaped for an audience are planned.
Read edited text back, refusing what it can't read.
Turn the edits a parse found into records, emitted together.

constructions.says: A new chain. Without of, the record is a root and starts a thing named by its own id.
Replaces x inside the thing both are of. Leave out of and it is refused, of-missing. Name a record of another thing and it is refused, prev-unrelated.
Naming every head leaves one head, unless another concurrent head remains.
Any kind may erase. x keeps its id, its signature and its place. Only its payload goes (the protocol calls it the opening).
Nobody's verb: a state. The thing has two heads, both shown, and the newer by content order is listed first.
Not a write at all: a view. The envelope still answers every test on it.

layers.name: Text
layers.gist: For an audience: what a lens renders, and what people edit.
layers.named: its base: the tick, the lens and the audience

layers.name: Tick
layers.gist: A result at a moment, covering exactly the records folded.
layers.named: an id over the vertex, what it covers and the result

layers.name: State
layers.gist: A vertex's slots, worked out from the set.
layers.lasts: a cache, worked out again at will

layers.name: View
layers.gist: What one reader holds, settled and admitted.
layers.named: nothing: it is the reader's own

layers.name: Store
layers.gist: A set of records in places. No order, no positions.
layers.lasts: as long as a place keeps it

layers.name: Record
layers.gist: The ground. Added, never edited. Only a payload can go.

rows.follow: its heads, or its live setters

refusals.note: Checked in this order. A field left out, or of the wrong JSON type, gets its own code.
Any string, anywhere in a record.
While a record is written one canonical way.
Shape, then labels, then writing, then prev-unknown, then under-unknown, then of-not-root, then prev-unrelated.
Before a tick's payload is read.
Named, with no test vector yet.

provenance.here: Every noun has one purpose, its own state and an operating principle: the three lines of each entry.
The grammar comes first, as nouns and verbs, and the object–action matrix shows where they meet.
Objects and operations only: no file formats, commands or screens.
The form: nouns, verbs and layers, each layer as high as it is temporary, and a walk taken step by step.
